Step P(k+1): state what must be proved

lines.text: Replace $1^2 + \cdots + k^2$ using the assumption $P(k)$.
$P(k+1)$ is true whenever $P(k)$ is true, and $P(1)$ is true. So the formula is true for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
P(n) is the statement $H(n) = (n+1)^2$.
This equals $H(1)=4$, so P(1) is true.

skill.title: Prove a divisibility result by induction
needs: Prove a series identity by induction

steps.title: Check the statement is true for n = 1

lines.text: 7 is divisible by 7, so the statement $P_1$ is true.

steps.title: Assume the statement is true for n = k

lines.text: Assume $8^k - 1$ is divisible by 7, so $8^k - 1 = 7M$ for some whole number $M$.
$8M + 1$ is a whole number, so $8^{k+1} - 1$ is divisible by 7.
$P_1$ is true, and if $P_k$ is true then $P_{k+1}$ is true. By induction, $8^n - 1$ is divisible by 7 for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

references.final: 8^n - 1 \text{ is divisible by } 7 \text{ for all } n \in \mathbb{N}

steps.title: Step P(1): test the first case

lines.text: Let $P(n)$ be the statement "$2^{3n-1}+3$ is divisible by 7".
$7$ is divisible by 7, so $P(1)$ is true.

steps.title: Step P(k): assume it is true for n = k

lines.text: Assume $2^{3k-1}+3$ is divisible by 7, so it equals $7M$ for some integer $M$.

steps.title: Step P(k+1): write the next case using 2^(3k-1)

lines.text: Replace $n$ with $k+1$: $3(k+1)-1 = 3k+2$.
Using $2^{3k-1} = 7M-3$ from the assumption:
This is a multiple of 7, so $P(k+1)$ is true.
$P(1)$ is true, and if $P(k)$ is true then $P(k+1)$ is true. Therefore $2^{3n-1}+3$ is divisible by 7 for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

references.final: 2^{3n-1}+3 \text{ is divisible by 7 for all } n \in \mathbb{N}
